newsitem.title: USA: Blue Chip Casino takes debt offering to shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Blue Chip Casino takes debt offering to shareholders.

text.p: Blue Chip Casino Inc will raise $80 million for the construction of its Michigan City, Indiana, riverboat via a private debt offering to its shareholders, according to an Indiana Gaming Commission spokeswoman.

The deal, approved by the commission this week, follows the cancellation of a planned $80 million junk bond offering from Blue Chip on March 19. The deal was to have been underwritten by lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
The new debt offering will be guaranteed by the Flynn group, which has a 53.23 percent stake in the gaming concern, the spokeswoman said.
"The Flynn group has agreed to buy all the debt that's not picked up by the shareholders and if that means taking all $80 million they will do that," she said.
Officials at Blue Chip Casino in Michigan City and in the Chicago area did not return numerous phone calls.

The initial $80 million offering via Merrill was to complement a $20 million private debt offering to shareholders that can now be eliminated due to projected savings through the private deal, the spokeswoman said.

The new private offering is expected to require a 16 percent interest rate compared to a 17.9 percent rate on the public deal, she added. The company also perceived savings in the elimination of a $10 million interest reserve, a $5 million construction completion reserve and $5 million in underwriting fees, the commission said.
Blue Chip was awarded the fifth gaming license in Northern Indiana and is expected to open a 34,000 square foot casino in Michigan City in August.
It has projected earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization near $29 million during its first full year of operations, a high-yield analyst said.
